# dist/grafana/ — reference dashboards & alert rules

Hand-maintained reference observability assets for the always-on
Prometheus `/metrics` endpoint both daemons expose (`GET /metrics`, the
open/unauthenticated route — see [`docs/admin/TELEMETRY.md`](../../docs/admin/TELEMETRY.md)).
These are **BYO-Prometheus** wiring: they pair with — they do not replace —
the daemon's own first-party email/webhook alerting
([`docs/admin/ALERTING.md`](../../docs/admin/ALERTING.md)).

Unlike the rest of `dist/`, these files are **not** generated by `build.rs`
— they are authored by hand and checked in.

## Contents

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `thurvtl-dashboard.json` | Grafana dashboard for Thur VTL (`thurvtl_*` metrics). |
| `thurvsa-dashboard.json` | Grafana dashboard for Thur VSA (`thurvsa_*` metrics). |
| `alerts.yaml` | Prometheus alerting rules (two groups, one per product). |

## Importing the dashboards

Grafana → Dashboards → New → Import → Upload the JSON. Each dashboard
declares a `${datasource}` template variable, so on import you pick which
Prometheus data source to bind it to; `$job` and `$backend` variables let
you scope to one daemon instance / storage backend. The dashboards assume
the daemon is scraped under a `job` label that starts with the product
name (`thurvtl` / `thurvsa`).

## Loading the alert rules

`alerts.yaml` holds **Prometheus** alerting rules, not Alertmanager
routing. Add the file to `rule_files:` in `prometheus.yml`:

```yaml
rule_files:
  - /etc/prometheus/rules/alerts.yaml
```

Prometheus evaluates the rules and forwards firing alerts to whatever
Alertmanager you have wired under `alerting.alertmanagers:`. Each rule
carries a `severity` label (`warning` / `critical`) and a `product` label
(`thurvtl` / `thurvsa`) for your Alertmanager routes to match on.

`promtool check rules alerts.yaml` validates the file if you have the
Prometheus toolkit installed.

## Regenerating the dashboards

The dashboards are emitted from a small generator kept out-of-tree (only
the JSON is checked in). If you change the metric surface, re-run the
generator and re-copy the JSON, then re-import. The header of each JSON
records the schema version it targets.
